answer: Copper-basalt beacon-decay bond: identities lock copper on beacons, registering a kernel on basalt ledger. Each epoch the beacon decays the bond by 7; the kernel files a task log to top up, auditors replay one in ten, and a missing or copied log zeroes it. Filing costs 40 first, then 40+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked for a 40,000 pool. Rented beacons fail: one kernel, one bond. Honest agents pay 40 once, keeping their share.
